rulings.barItem: vendor behaviour the vendor's documentation contradicts
rulings.reason: Steps 25, 56 and 100 expect POST /2/tweets to answer 400 "real X surface this twin does not model" for reply_settings "following", community_id with share_with_followers true, and made_with_ai true. X documents all three as valid request fields: the vendored X API v2 document (spec/openapi.json.gz, 2.168, CreatePostsRequest: reply_settings enum following/mentionedUsers/subscribers/verified, community_id, share_with_followers, made_with_ai boolean; https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/create-post), and X's changelog (https://docs.x.com/changelog, 28 Jul 2025: a post with community_id and share_with_followers: true is also broadcast to followers). A twin's gap is not X's answer, and a life step never asserts it as one; the step names admit it. Steps 95 to 99 upload and process a third copy of the recording only for step 100's refused submission, so that post is promised and never made.
rulings.correction: Expect X's 201 for each of the three posts (the twin models reply_settings, community_id with share_with_followers and made_with_ai), dropping step 26's second post of the devlog text once step 25 publishes it; or remove steps 25, 56 and 95 to 100 from the life.

rulings.barItem: vendor behaviour the vendor's documentation contradicts
rulings.reason: Step 69 replies to {p1}, Volter's own devlog post, from Volter's own account and expects 403 because "the original post did not summon Volter". X's summons rule (https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/manage-tweets/introduction, "Replies are only permitted if the original post's author has explicitly summoned the replying account"; https://docs.x.com/changelog, 23 Feb 2026) restricts replies to other authors' posts; on X's own developer forum (https://devcommunity.x.com/t/restricting-programmatic-replies-does-this-affect-replying-to-itself/257955) replying to your own post is answered as unaffected, which is how a thread is made. The author of {p1} is the replier.
rulings.correction: Expect 201 for the auto-plug reply to the account's own post, capturing its id.

rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept
rulings.reason: Step 5 makes @mira_builds protected and no step has @volterai follow her; step 64 has her reply to the devlog, and step 70 has Ines 'follow Mira's reply from its notification'. X's Help Center (https://help.x.com/en/safety-and-security/public-and-protected-posts) states that replies a protected account sends to an account that is not following it will not be seen by that account, so no notification of the reply reaches @volterai. Step 70 also carries no session cookie, though a notification is read signed in.
rulings.correction: Remove "protected": true from step 5 and remove step 70 (Mira's question is then public, as act 4 tells it).

rulings.barItem: a date that contradicts the `wait` steps
rulings.reason: Step 71's wait (3h after 14:30 UTC) lands at 17:30 UTC on 10 June, which is 13:30 in New York, where Volter and Ines work and where every launch act names its hours; the step calls it 'That evening'.
rulings.correction: Make step 71's wait `480m` (18:30 New York) and step 78's wait `6270m`, so Monday 15 June keeps its 07:00 UTC.

rulings.barItem: a state switched away and back in one sitting, or returned with no reason the story shows
rulings.reason: The X channel was connected on 9 June (steps 20 and 21) and nothing revoked it; X's OAuth 1.0a access tokens 'do not expire but can be revoked by the user at any time' (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-1-0a/obtaining-user-access-tokens). Steps 72 to 74 reconnect the same account the same afternoon 'while cleaning up her draft queue', which is no reason to re-authorize, and replace the working token with an identical grant only to reach the remembered-approval redirect.
rulings.correction: Remove steps 72 to 74 and keep step 21's access token and secret for the later Scheduler calls.

rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept
rulings.reason: Step 79 reopens 'her old consent tab' with {rt}, which at that point is step 72's request token; step 73 redirected straight to Scheduler for it, so no consent screen for that token was ever shown. Nothing in the 15 June recording act gives Ines a reason to open an authenticate URL six days later; the refusal exists to reach the invalid-token page.

rulings.barItem: a feature tour: one call per option of an endpoint in a row
rulings.reason: Steps 75, 76 and 77 are three GET /2/users/by/username/{username} lookups in a row reaching the endpoint's 400, 200 and not-found-in-200 answers (getUsersByUsername in the vendored X API v2 document, spec/openapi.json.gz). Step 77's mistyped handle comes after step 76 has already found @mira_builds, so the search has no purpose in the story.

rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept
rulings.reason: Steps 75 and 76 look up Mira so that Ines can credit her in 'her next draft', but no Scheduler post ever carries @mira_builds: the next post (step 94) is the recording, without her. Step 76 also calls her 'the artist who answered the devlog', but in the story she is an audience member who asked whether it runs on Linux (step 64). X's mention is made by the post's text (https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/manage-tweets/introduction).
rulings.correction: After step 76, add the POST /2/tweets that publishes the draft whose text credits @mira_builds for what she did (answering the devlog's question), and name her as a reader rather than an artist; or remove steps 75 and 76.

rulings.barItem: content that does not bear out the step's name
rulings.reason: Steps 120 and 124 'open verification again' through Dub, but they reopen step 115's authorize URL, with its state Kq7mB2xVn_4dLs9T and its code_challenge, and steps 121 and 125 expect that state back while step 126 sends the first code_verifier. Dub at 7e0101363b2a mints a new state (nanoid(16), kept in Redis for 5 minutes) and a new PKCE verifier (a 5-minute cookie) on every start (apps/web/lib/actions/partners/start-partner-platform-verification.ts), and its callback deletes the state before the token exchange and redirects without exchanging when the state is missing or expired (apps/web/app/(ee)/api/partners/platforms/callback/route.ts). Step 125 returns that state 31 minutes after it was minted and after step 122's callback deleted it, so Dub would never make step 126's exchange. X's PKCE flow (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-2-0/authorization-code) checks a code against the challenge of its own authorization request.
rulings.correction: Give each restart its own authorize URL, with a new state and code_challenge, expect that state back on its redirect, and send the verifier of the attempt being completed in the exchange.

rulings.barItem: a refusal without a cause the story shows, or the same cause drawn twice; a run of refusals
rulings.reason: In one sitting, Kestrel's verification fails twice for the same cause, Volter's unfinished Dub-for-X setup. First the console still holds the preview callback (step 113, which step 9 shows). Then the deployment still holds placeholder client keys (step 122, which no earlier step shows). The literal '%' client id is chosen to reach RFC 6749 section 2.3.1's malformed-credential 400, which X's token page (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-2-0/user-access-token) never describes. No customer has a reason to make that refusal.
rulings.correction: Keep steps 113 and 114, remove steps 122 to 125 (the placeholder exchange, the 30m wait and the second consent), and let step 126 exchange step 121's code.

rulings.barItem: content that does not bear out the step's name
rulings.reason: Step 147 claims Ines 'copies an incomplete post number from Aaron's message', but it requests /AaronYEtc/status/9999999999999999999, nineteen nines that are no part of {launch}. Its handle is correctly cased, although the act has her type it lowercased. It is also sent without the x-forwarded-prefix and sec-fetch-dest headers, so it is not at the World's place, where every other launch step and x.com's post address (x.com/<handle>/status/<id>) are.
rulings.correction: Capture a truncated prefix of the launch id from step 140's location (for example `"launchcut": "header:location:posted=([0-9]{12})"`), request /aaronyetc/status/{launchcut} and send it with the place's x-forwarded-prefix and sec-fetch-dest headers.
